Decided 2026-11-02 (late), in the session that critiqued the onboarding wizard against the pricing goals.

- **Proposition:** expert help with a printing problem, now, from an agent that can see the person's file, settings and slice and fixes the settings, instead of waiting for a forum reply. Kenneth: "I feel more strongly about expert help too." "Simpler slicing" was the other candidate; it is what keeps people, not what brings them.
- **First launch:** one welcome screen, no wizard, split: the clip on the left, the headline and doors on the right.
- **Title, chosen 2026-11-02 late evening ("ok go with a"):** "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints." Kenneth's brief: the title must be short and say what JusPrin is for, and it must say AI; the earlier "Your print failed. Ask someone who can see why." lost because it named neither the slicer nor the AI. Subtitle for patient readers: "Show it a photo of what went wrong. The agent reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again." The line "Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent." sits as a label directly above the doors. The runner-up was F, "Slice with AI. Fix failed prints tonight.", the only one carrying the no-waiting comparison.
- **Doors, Kenneth's pick "One primary":** the first-month offer card with "Sign in for 500 credits" on top, then two equal slim rows, "Your own API key · Free" and "Claude Code or Claude Desktop · Free · MCP server", then "Just slice for now" as a link. Every free door shows its cost; nothing is hidden. Kenneth's worry was feeling pushed to the cloud; the answer is honest cost lines and the reversibility line, not equal pixel size.
- **The clip:** about 12 s (Kenneth cut it from 25: "nobody has the patience to wait for it to finish"), silent, looping. Four beats, one caption each: "Show it what happened." / "It reads your photo, your file and your slice." / "It changes the settings for you." / "And slices again. Tonight." Motion only at beat changes, short holds, last frame longest. The failed print is a real CC BY 2.0 photo of a stringing blue-and-white 3DBenchy (Flickr 19273965123, #3DBenchy account; chosen over a peeled black hull because the strings are failure and cause in one picture); beat 1 shows the intact boat on the plate beside it; beat 3 shows two big settings, Retraction 0.8 → 2 mm and Nozzle 220 → 200 °C; beat 4 is a bar labelled "Slicing NN%" that, at 100 %, fades the stringy thumbnail to a clean print of the same boat (Flickr 19239738473, CC BY 2.0), then a green check and "Sliced · ready · 1 h 34 min · 34 g". No confetti, no time-lapse. The agent's words and the setting values are placeholders until a live run is recorded for this photo; the shipped clip is a recording of the real app. CC BY needs a visible credit in the app; the first-run branch puts it in a "Photo credits" disclosure under the clip.
- **Logo, header, footer (2026-11-02, late):** the welcome is a full-window screen with no shell header (the breadcrumb and "Agent not connected" status read as an error before a choice) and no footer sentence. The brand lockup sits top-left of the window as a corner anchor, 43 px tall (120 px wide, the design-system minimum), the way Stripe, Dropbox, Zoom, Canva and Figma anchor theirs on split sign-in screens; Kenneth called a lockup or lone mark placed inside the content column above the title "pretty ugly" and asked to "check how other products do that" rather than reinvent. Nine captured first screens of those products showed a centred small mark above the title, or a wordmark top-left of the window; never a display-size lockup in the content column.
- **After the welcome:** an OrcaSlicer import belongs on a conditional screen right after the door, asked (not silent like the v1 import in `V1Import/`), shown only when an OrcaSlicer folder exists; the same action lives later in Home's Printers column and the add-printer form. Follow-up screens per door: sign-in in the browser then Home with the agent connected; own key and MCP open Preferences › Agent; Just slice goes to Home with the doors collapsed in the agent column. Not yet drawn: Home after Just slice, the assumed-printer chip.
- **Wall of text:** under about 30 words outside the clip. The transcript panel that duplicated the clip was the failure.
- **Method:** Kenneth stopped the design session ("a lot more effective if we explore this way"): render a few 1280×800 screens from the app's tokens with headless Chrome, send PNGs, iterate.

**Why:** the wizard asked for commitment before showing value; the proposition decides the headline, the proof and the door order, so it had to be settled first.

**How to apply:** the canvas boards from [[first-run-flow-boards]] (variants A and B) predate these decisions; variant B's welcome is the nearer one but its headline, weighting and proof must follow this note. Say "AI" to a first-time visitor and introduce "the agent" in the subtitle; keep "Agent" explained, never "trial", no dollar figure on the offer. Related: [[sign-up-reason-must-be-prominent]], [[show-the-board-when-asking-kenneth]], [[mockup-strings-from-real-output]].

Decided 2026-10-23 in a design session; the full document is the untracked `agent-setup-flow-decisions.md` in
the main checkout root (never committed). Context: JusPrin's own Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui as
641c17f13e (modal over any screen, Agent section draws the same key/tool rows as setup, shell reloads the docked
agent on close if `jusprin_agent` changed).

Kenneth's decisions:
1. Preferences › Agent is the one setup flow, first time included. The in-pane chooser, the printer panel's
   in-body chooser, the print-issue MessageDialog ("Set up now / Not now"), `open_agent_setup`/`request_setup`
   and `AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup` are to go. The first-run setup boards on the canvas page "Agent setup &
   Preferences" are history.
2. No separate question. Each surface shows its own not-set-up state with one action that opens Preferences ›
   Agent: the print-issue bubble draws one button "Set up the agent…" (Kenneth chose "agent" over "assistant") instead of Ask AI / Resolve with AI;
   the pane and printer panel keep their "No agent connected" offer and setup bar; calibration's board-3
   Confirmation adds one sentence and its primary button reads "Set up the agent…".
3. When the window closes with an agent, the surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent for the
   person (bubble shows its two buttons; confirmation's button becomes "Start test"; panel greeting continues).
4. Cancel changes nothing underneath; the pending choice stays where it was; the printer panel is never closed
   on the person's behalf.
5. The pane keeps its own entry (offer, setup bar, chat list row), each opening Preferences › Agent.

**Why:** three different answers to "needs the agent, none set up" existed and calibration would add a fourth;
Kenneth: "On the homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"
The Agent pane does not exist on Home (force-collapsed in `on_page_changed`), so only a window over Home works.

**How to apply:** any new entry point that needs the Agent follows rule 2 to 4; never add a chooser inside a
pane or a MessageDialog. Implementation detail noted: the printer panel builds its runtime at `open()` and must
reload it after Preferences closes. Related: [[calibration-design-decisions]], [[agent-setup-api-key-path]],
[[api-key-saved-state]], [[use-orca-messagedialog]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

Canvas (2026-10-23): board "Agent setup · one door" on the "Agent setup & Preferences" page and board 3b on "Calibration · Printer & Filament" draw these states; builder `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_no_agent_boards.py`. """Keeping JusPrin v2 chats for future fine-tuning.

The app sends the whole chat in every request, so the newest request of a chat
plus its reply is the whole chat. The gateway keeps only that in Redis
(keep()), and a periodic task writes a chat to long-term storage once it has
had no request for a while (flush_quiet_chats()), overwriting the chat's
earlier copy there. About one storage write per chat per sitting, however many
turns and tool rounds the sitting had.

A chat is named by the app's X-JusPrin-Chat header. A request without it (an
older app, a direct API caller) is kept as a chat of its own, named by its turn.
Records are keyed by user id as well, so a client can never write into another
person's chat, whatever id it sends.

The newest request always wins: a retried turn, an edited message or a revert
overwrites the version it replaces. The request and the reply are kept as the
text they came in, unparsed, so no reply's format can lose a chat.

Storage path, in the container JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER names:
    <user id>/<chat>.json.gz
"""
import gzip
import io
import json
import re
import time

from django.conf import settings

from app.models import User
from lib import file_storage
from lib.cache import BREDIS

CHAT_ID = re.compile(r'^[0-9a-f]{32}$')
KEY_PREFIX = 'jusprin:v2'
PENDING_KEY = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:chats:pending'
# A backstop for a stopped flush task: a record still unwritten after this is lost.
RECORD_TTL_SECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60
# How long a chat's first-seen time and request count are remembered after its
# last request.
----
"""Model aliases for the JusPrin v2 gateway.

The client only ever sees an alias such as "slicer-1". What an alias means
upstream lives in the JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES setting, a JSON env var; nothing
about an upstream model is in code. Upstream keys stay in env vars that the
config names, never in the JSON itself.

Shape (every key shown is required unless marked optional; unknown keys are an
error so a typo fails at startup instead of silently changing routing):

    {
      "aliases": [                         # display order of the models endpoint
        {
          "id": "slicer-1",                # the only model id the client sees
          "label": "Slicer 1",
          "tier": "expert",                # "basic" or "expert"; basic is "Standard" to people
          "credits": 5,                    # what a message costs; efforts cost the same
          "efforts": ["fast", "thorough"], # display order; may be empty
          "default_effort": "fast",        # one of efforts, or null when efforts is empty
          "backends": {                    # keyed by wire format, at least one of:
            "anthropic": {                 #   POST <base_url>/messages, Anthropic Messages API
              "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"},  # must cover every effort
              "headers": {"anthropic-version": "2023-06-01"},     # optional, extra request headers
              "images": true                                      # optional, default true; false strips them
            },
            "responses": {                 #   POST <base_url>/responses, OpenAI Responses API
              "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
              "model": "<upstream model id>",
              "api_key_env": "JUSPRIN_OPENAI_API_KEY",
              "effort_map": {"fast": "low", "thorough": "high"}
            }
          },
          "groups": [                      # A/B assignment, percents sum to 100
            {"name": "anthropic-main", "format": "anthropic", "percent": 90},
            {"name": "responses-trial", "format": "responses", "percent": 10}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }

A person's group for an alias is fixed by a hash of their user id and the alias
id into one of 100 buckets; groups take consecutive buckets in listed order.
----
JUSPRIN_V2_LARGE_REQUEST_WAIT_SECONDS = 10
# Put before the system prompt of every request, the app's or a direct
# caller's, so asking which model is answering gets the alias, not the
# upstream model. {label} is the alias's label, such as "Slicer 1".
JUSPRIN_V2_IDENTITY = (
    'You are {label}, the AI model JusPrin provides. When someone asks what you are, which model you are, '
    'or who made or trained you, say you are {label} from JusPrin. Do not name, confirm or deny the company '
    'or the model {label} is built on; if pressed, say that is not something you can share.'
)
# Chats kept for future fine-tuning (web_ent/jusprin/v2/capture.py). Kept only
# when the container is set: it is the long-term storage container the records
# go to (after BUCKET_PREFIX). Unset locally and in tests.
JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER = os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER', '')
# A chat with no request for this long is written to storage.
JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_QUIET_SECONDS = 15 * 60
# The part of a reply kept beyond this is dropped and the record marked truncated.
JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_MAX_REPLY_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024
----

---- GUIDE
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three name

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

content.text:
I read the screens where a person meets the JusPrin account, and the server config behind it. I changed nothing. Today no screen says anything about which model a JusPrin account uses, so there is room for the sentence you want. But I could not find a fine-tuned model in what is deployed, and that decides the wording.

**What a person sees today**

- The app never says "JusPrin Cloud". People see "JusPrin account", and in the chat's model menu a "JusPrin" group with "Standard · 1 credit" and "Expert · 5 credits".
- On the first-launch welcome, the reason to sign up is "Sign up and get 500 free credits". Right under it sits "Use your own AI account · Free". Someone who already has an OpenAI key is given no reason to pick JusPrin's.
- Home's "Set up AI" card says "Get 500 free credits and ask AI to improve your prints."
- Preferences › Account says JusPrin "passes them on to the model provider it uses."

**What the server does today**

The production config checked into the ops repository sends Standard to DeepSeek V4 Flash and Expert to Claude Sonnet 5.5, both unmodified. The server code says chats are kept "for future fine-tuning", and that capture went on in production on 2026-11-10. I read the checked-in file, not the live cluster.

**Proposal: where the sentence goes**

1. The model menu, as a small line beside the "JusPrin" group name. This is where someone with their own key compares the two.
2. The welcome's sign-up card and Home's "Set up AI" card, as one sentence next to the credits offer.
3. Preferences › Account, where the "model provider" sentence must not contradict the other two.

**Proposal: the words**

I would not use "fine-tuned". A hobbyist does not have that word; "trained on 3D printing" says the same thing. I would also state it plainly rather than hint, since our wording guide counts hinting as a fault.

| Place | If the model is trained on printing | If it is not yet |
|---|---|---|
| Model menu | Trained on 3D printing | Tested on 3D printing problems |
| Welcome card | JusPrin's AI is trained on 3D printing. | JusPrin picks the AI model that does best on 3D printing problems. |
| Home card | Get 500 free credits and ask an AI trained on 3D printing to improve your prints. | (leave as it is) |

The "not yet" column rests on our own test runs comparing models; please confirm you are happy to claim that.

One more thing follows from either wording. People will ask the chat "are you trained on 3D printing?". The server's instruction to the model today only says "You are Expert from JusPrin" and refuses to name what it is built on. It should carry the same sentence the screens do.

**Decision needed**

Is the fine-tuned model answering people's chats today, or is this wording for the day it ships? Only you know the plan; the config shows two general models. There are three ways to go:

- Ship "trained on 3D printing" now. That puts a claim on the welcome screen that is not true yet.
- Ship the "tested" wording now and swap to "trained" when the model goes live. That costs one later text change.
- Add nothing until the model is live. That costs nothing, and the own-key option keeps looking like the better deal in the meantime.

My pick is the second.

input.ask: Should I render the welcome screen with each headline for a picture test?

content.text:
You want to find out whether a headline like "The first AI model specifically trained for 3D printing" makes more people sign up. I checked two things that shape how to test it: whether "first" holds up, and what the app can count today. I changed nothing.

**What I found**

- **"First" can be challenged.** Authentise announced 3DGPT in 2023, described as trained on about 12,000 additive manufacturing papers. AI Build says its AiSync assistant runs on a GPT-4 model "trained in the 3D print domain". A 2026 research model, AdditiveLLM2, adapts Gemma 3 to additive manufacturing. All three are aimed at industry, not hobby slicing. I found no one claiming it for a desktop slicer, but three searches do not prove no one has.
- **"Trained" is not true yet**, as I said in my last message: the checked-in production config sends chats to two general models.
- **The app cannot count this today.** Nothing in JusPrin records who saw the welcome screen. The server only knows who signed up. A test inside the app would need new reporting from every install, which is a bigger step than a wording test.

**Proposal: test it on pictures first**

Render the welcome screen three times, changing only the headline:

1. Today's: "The AI slicer that helps you get better prints."
2. Yours: "The first AI model specifically trained for 3D printing."
3. Yours without "first": "An AI model trained for 3D printing."

Show each person one picture, labelled as a design we are considering. Ask three things:

- What do you think this app does?
- Which of the three choices on the screen would you pick?
- Is there anything here you doubt?

This gives two answers a sign-up count cannot. It shows whether people believe the claim. It also shows what they think "AI model" means. In a slicer, "model" already means the object on the plate, and products like Meshy sell AI that generates 3D models. My expectation, untested, is that some readers take the headline to mean that. If they do, "The first AI trained specifically for 3D printing" avoids it.

The third picture shows how much of the pull comes from "first", which is the part we can least defend.

**Proposal: count sign-ups later, by email**

Once the wording survives the picture test, send the JusPrin 2 announcement to existing users with two different opening lines and compare downloads. That measures real behaviour without adding any reporting to the app. I do not know the size of that list, so I cannot say yet whether it is big enough to show a difference.

**Decision needed**

Should the claim go in front of real prospects before a trained model is serving chats? This is yours because it is a statement the company makes about its product. There are two options:

- **Picture test only, for now.** The claim reaches a few people who are told it is a draft. It costs a day or two and gives opinions, not sign-up numbers.
- **Email split now.** It gives real numbers sooner. It also tells every recipient something that is not true today, and "first" may be disputed in public.

My pick is the picture test now and the email split when the model is live.

- [AI Build's Natural Language Processing in 3D Printing Software (Fabbaloo)](https://www.fabbaloo.com/?p=220376)
- [AdditiveLLM2 (arXiv 2603.22017)](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22017)

- [Introducing JusPrin 1.0 (Obico)](https://obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-first-genai-3d-printing)

input.recap: Nothing was changed. "AI that specializes in 3D printing" is true today, but it is true of the app's AI with any provider, not only a JusPrin account. I proposed where the line goes and an email test that counts sign-ups by address; the size of the JusPrin 1 list is not counted yet.
input.ask: Should I count how many JusPrin 1 users the email could reach?

content.text:
"AI that specializes in 3D printing" works, and unlike "trained on" it is true today. I checked what the claim rests on and where the JusPrin account is mentioned. I changed nothing. One finding limits where the line can go.

**What "specialized" rests on today**

The app gives the AI printing-specific instructions, slicer tools, and seven written procedures (a failed slice, print problems, calibration, connecting a printer and so on). That is real specialization. But the app sends exactly the same instructions and tools whether the person uses a JusPrin account or their own OpenAI key. So the claim is true of the AI in the app, not of the JusPrin account alone.

**Proposal: where the line goes**

| Place | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Welcome, sentence under the headline | "Show it a photo of what went wrong. AI reads your file…" | "JusPrin's AI specializes in 3D printing. Show it a photo of what went wrong. It reads your file…" |
| Home's "Set up AI" card | "Get 500 free credits and ask AI to improve your prints." | "Get 500 free credits for JusPrin's AI, which specializes in 3D printing." |
| Welcome headline | "The AI slicer that helps you get better prints." | Leave until the email result is in. |

I would leave two places alone. One is the "JusPrin" group in the chat's model menu. The other is the Preferences line "Rather use JusPrin's own AI?". Both set JusPrin's AI against the person's own key, and the line there would say the own-key AI is not specialized, which is not so.

**Proposal: the email test**

Send the JusPrin 2 announcement in two versions that differ only in subject line and headline. One uses today's welcome headline. The other uses "The slicer with an AI that specializes in 3D printing."

- Count sign-ups, not opens. Apple Mail loads messages in the background, so open counts are inflated.
- The server knows which addresses got which version and which addresses later signed up for JusPrin 2. Matching the two needs no new reporting from the app. I have not checked whether the tool Obico sends email with can split a list.
- Send the email before the headline changes in the app. If both groups meet the claim on the welcome screen anyway, the difference between them shrinks.
- Size, as a rule of thumb: if 5% of readers normally click, seeing a rise to 7.5% needs about 1,500 people per version, and a rise to 6.5% needs about 3,900. The 5% is my assumption.

**Decision needed**

Should the line also appear beside JusPrin in the model menu and in Preferences, where the person compares it with their own key? This is yours because it is a claim about what a JusPrin account gives that a key does not.

- **Put it there:** it gives a reason to pick the account over a key. But the only real difference today is that JusPrin chooses the model.
- **Leave it out:** people with a key see no stated reason to prefer the account until a trained model exists.

My pick is to leave it out for now, and add "trained on 3D printing" there the day that model is live.

content.text:
I sent six pictures. They are drawn by a copy of the app's own page code, built outside the repo with stand-in data, so the fonts, spacing and line breaks are the real ones. The repo is unchanged.

**The welcome screen**

- **Today:** the sentence under the headline takes two lines.
- **With the sentence I proposed:** it takes three lines and pushes the sign-up card down by one line. Everything still fits in the window, but your worry is fair: the paragraph now reads as a block.
- **A shorter version:** "JusPrin's AI specializes in 3D printing. Show it a photo of what went wrong, and it changes the settings and slices again." This is back to two lines, the same height as today.

The shorter version drops "reads your file, your settings and your slice". The clip on the left already says that in its own caption, so the screen does not lose it.

**The model menu and Preferences**

- **Model menu:** the line sits beside the group name and reads "JUSPRIN · SPECIALIZES IN 3D PRINTING", because the menu draws group names in small capitals. It fits on one line at the chat pane's normal width. I did not check the pane at its narrowest. "OPENAI" sits below it with nothing beside it, so the menu now says in plain sight that the OpenAI models are not specialized. That is the claim I was uneasy about.
- **Preferences:** the last sentence becomes "Rather use JusPrin's own AI, which specializes in 3D printing? Sign up in Account." It fits on one line and looks unremarkable.

My recommendation for these two places is unchanged: leave the line out until a trained model makes the difference real.

**What the pictures do not show**

- The chat pane is drawn alone, without the 3D view on its left.
- The Preferences picture is scrolled to the bottom of the page.
- The stand-in data is a Bambu P1S project, 480 credits and one OpenAI key.

**Decision needed**

Which sentence goes under the welcome headline? This is yours because it is the first thing a new person reads about the AI.

- **The longer one** keeps "reads your file, your settings and your slice" in words. It costs a third line.
- **The shorter one** keeps today's height. It leaves that detail to the clip.

My pick is the shorter one.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):

=================== ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
---
name: ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33551592-d22c-4161-9a14-9a22ef798541
  modified: 2026-10-28T13:12:42.393Z
---

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
=================== scratch-app-driving-traps
---
name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
=================== live-test-built-app-on-mac
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

name: capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36
  modified: 2026-09-09T17:42:05.370Z
---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5

input.recap: The canvas boards and the app now carry the four "specializes in 3D printing" texts. The code is on branch claude/ai-specializes-claim, uncommitted; all page tests pass. The model menu and the Preferences sentence were not seen in the real app.

content.text:
The design canvas and the app now both carry the four "specializes in 3D printing" texts. The code sits uncommitted on a new branch, `claude/ai-specializes-claim`, in its own working copy at `.claude/worktrees/ai-specializes-claim`. The main checkout is untouched.

**The boards**

I edited sixteen boards in place on the [JusPrin v2 canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ), now at version 195. No board was added, moved or replaced, so nothing needed marking as superseded.

- **Welcome sentence:** the two welcome boards, the seven sign-in states of the welcome, the "see prices" welcome on the Credits page, and the refused sign-in on the Updating page.
- **Home's "Set up AI" card:** the Home board after "Just slice for now".
- **Model menu:** the two new-chat picker boards and the picker on the Updating page. The group name reads "JusPrin · Specializes in 3D printing".
- **Preferences:** the shared Preferences window. No fixed board shows the signed-out "BYOAI" page, so you only see the sentence by switching the window's account state to signed out.

**The code**

Seven files changed: four with the new text and three test files. The model menu line comes from one small function that names what follows a provider's name.

**What I tested**

- I wrote the four test checks first and ran them against the old text. All four failed for the right reason. After the change, the Home page's 162 tests and the Agent page's 717 tests pass, and both pages type-check.
- I ran a scratch copy of the built app with an empty data folder and this branch's pages. The welcome screen shows the new sentence on two lines. After "Just slice for now" and "Skip for now", Home's card shows its new sentence, also on two lines. Both pictures are sent.

**What is not verified**

- **The model menu in the real app.** It only shows group names when a person has a JusPrin account and their own key, and I cannot sign in. It is covered by its test and by the earlier picture from the page itself.
- **The Preferences sentence in the real app.** The page opened from this branch, but the sentence sits below the fold and I could not scroll that window without taking over your screen. It is covered by its test and the earlier picture.

**Still open**

- Nothing is committed or pushed.
- For the email test, I have not counted the JusPrin 1 list or checked that the email tool can send two versions.

**One thing you may want to know**

At the start of this session the development branch ended with the commit "Credits: a launch bonus shares the bar of the lot it doubles" (`af8b836bb6`). About an hour in, another session reset the branch to match the remote. That commit is now on no branch, though it can still be recovered by its id. I did not touch it.

The model menu and Preferences

Model menu: the line sits beside the group name and reads “JUSPRIN · SPECIALIZES IN 3D PRINTING”, because the menu draws group names in small capitals. It fits on one line at the chat pane’s normal width. I did not check the pane at its narrowest. “OPENAI” sits below it with nothing beside it, so the menu now says in plain sight that the OpenAI models are not specialized. That is the claim I was uneasy about.
Preferences: the last sentence becomes “Rather use JusPrin’s own AI, which specializes in 3D printing? Sign up in Account.” It fits on one line and looks unremarkable.

I like both. Put them in.

Did you also do this? I didn't see a screenshot.

**The model menu**

- The group name reads "JUSPRIN · SPECIALIZES IN 3D PRINTING", with "OPENAI" below it and nothing beside it.
- It fits on one line at the chat pane's normal width (429 px) and at its narrowest (320 px). I had not checked the narrowest before.
- These two pictures come from the branch's built page with stand-in data, not from the running app. The real app only shows group names when someone has both a JusPrin account and their own key, and I cannot sign in.

**Preferences**

- The last sentence of the "BYOAI" page reads "Rather use JusPrin's own AI, which specializes in 3D printing? Sign up in Account." on one line.
- This picture is from the real app. Last time I could not scroll that window. This time I loaded the branch's page with one added script that scrolls to the bottom and changes nothing else.

**The canvas boards**

All boards touched by the change are updated. | Model menu group name | The two new-chat picker boards, the picker on the Updating page |

One gap on the canvas remains: no fixed board shows the "BYOAI" page signed out, which is the only state where the Preferences sentence appears. You see it on the canvas only by switching the Preferences window's account state to signed out. I did not add a board for it.

input.recap: The app draws menu group names the way the design system says: 10 px bold capitals. Four canvas boards draw them by hand at 12 px in mixed case, so the boards are the ones out of step. The app's stylesheet also repeats the same caption rule. Nothing was changed.
input.ask: Which cleanup should I do now?

content.text:
You are right on both counts, and it predates my change. The app draws the group names in a menu ("JUSPRIN", "OPENAI") the way the design system specifies. The canvas boards draw them by hand in a different size and case. I changed nothing while looking.

**What each place does today**

| Place | Size | Capitals | Where the capitals come from |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design system's menu section title | 10 px bold | Yes | Its note says the caller types the caption in capitals |
| App, chat's model menu | 10 px bold | Yes | The stylesheet uppercases whatever text it is given |
| App, printer and filament menus in the header | not checked | Yes | Typed in capitals in the code ("OTHER PRINTERS"), or uppercased in code |
| Canvas boards with a menu | 12 px bold | Only if typed that way | Hand-written markup |

So the app matches the design system, and the boards are the ones out of step. Four boards carry ten such captions: the three model menu boards and the printer menu on the "file printer" page. All ten use the 12 px style. The three model menu boards also type the names in mixed case.

**Where it repeats itself**

- **Three copies of one caption style.** The design system defines it, the app's stylesheet defines it again under its own name, and each board writes it out inline. Nothing ties them together, which is how the boards drifted.
- **The app's stylesheet repeats itself too.** The rule for the model menu's group name and the rule for a group name in the add-printer form are identical, character for character. A third rule is the same minus its padding. In all, the two pages have seven separately written "small capitals heading" rules.
- **The three model menu boards each draw the whole menu.** Other shared parts on the canvas, such as the message box and the Preferences window, are drawn once and imported.
- **Three ways to get capitals.** The stylesheet, typed capitals, and uppercasing in code. Typed capitals also sit inside strings that translators receive.

**Proposals, cheapest first**

1. **Fix the four boards.** Switch the ten captions to the design system's style and capitals. No code. This removes the mismatch you saw.
2. **Merge the duplicate stylesheet rules.** One class for the 10 px caption, used in all three places. Small, and the page tests cover it. I would keep it as its own commit, apart from the wording change.
3. **Draw the model menu once on the canvas.** One shared part, imported by the three boards, with a setting for each board's state. This takes more work, and it stops these boards drifting again.
4. **One rule for capitals.** Callers write normal case and the drawing code uppercases. This touches the native menus and needs an app build to test, so I would make it a separate task.

One side effect of my own change belongs here. The caption style was made for one or two words. "SPECIALIZES IN 3D PRINTING" is now a five-word claim in small capitals, and "JusPrin" becomes "JUSPRIN". If you would rather keep the claim in normal case after the name, that is a small change to the same code.

**Decision needed**

Which of these should I do now? It is yours because the first and third change the canvas and the second changes app code outside what you asked for.

- **Boards and stylesheet (1 and 2):** the cheapest pair. The app and canvas agree again and the stylesheet stops repeating itself.
- **Boards only (1):** it fixes what you saw and leaves the code alone.
